title: Pico Onramp Chefbook — labnotes & boot heuristics (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, session-first "chefbook" for bootstrapping new internal adopters onto the Redwood SDK in under 15 minutes. Target audience: platform integrators, solutions engineers, and devs doing quick POCs. Tone: workshop/lab notes — choppy, prescriptive, and intentionally terse.

Summary (TL;DR):
- 12-minute microflow to get a toy app running (TypeScript + local emulator)
- 3 starter recipes (chat UI, embed+search, rerank pipeline)
- Pseudocode init for TS/Python with recommended telemetry hooks
- A tiny docker-based sandbox recipe for offline demo sessions
- Checklist of failure modes and recovery commands

Session microflow — "12-minute quicksmith":
(aim: demo-ready toy app)
1) Prereqs (1 min): node 18, python 3.10, docker optional, Redwood API key (dev scope).
2) Clone lightweight starter: git clone github.com/redwood-inference/pico-starter && cd pico-starter (30s)
3) Install + env (1 min): npm i && cp .env.example .env && set REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxx
4) Minimal server (2 min): Start the tiny express wrapper that forwards prompts to Redwood hosted endpoint.
5) Minimal client (3 min): open index.html, swap demo prompt, run demo.
6) Telemetry & smoke (3.5 min): enable sdk telemetry sample rate = 0.1, trigger 5 requests, inspect /telemetry/events in devtools or local log.
7) Wrap + next steps (1 min): add embed pipeline or turn on dedicated model variant.

Starter recipes (short):
- Chat UI: instructions to wire streaming + tool-calling skeleton, fallback to short-mode model when latency >150ms. Notes about prefix caching and token budgeting.
- Embed + search: local SQLite vector index recipe (faiss-lite), embedding batching heuristics, warmup tips to avoid cold quantized model startup.
- Rerank pipeline: call candidate-gen (smaller model) -> embed -> rerank (medium model) with explicit request-id propagation and deterministic seed for offline repro.

Pseudocode — TypeScript init snippet:

// minimal SDK bootstrap (pseudo)
import {RedwoodClient} from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: 'us-west-2', telemetry: { sampleRate: 0.1 } });
async function runChat(prompt){
  const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'rwd-chat-small-v1', messages: [{role:'user',content:prompt}], maxTokens: 256 });
  stream.on('delta', d => renderChunk(d.text));
  stream.on('done', () => flushTrace());
}

Pseudocode — Python init snippet:
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'], telemetry={'sample_rate':0.1})
def one_shot(prompt):
    resp = client.generate(prompt, model='rwd-text-embed-01', max_tokens=128)
    return resp.text

Mini sandbox (docker compose)
- Services: nginx static demo, node proxy (dev key), sqlite vector store, local telemetry collector (simple logstash).
- Purpose: airgapped demo where hosted keys are not used; run local emulation of Redwood behavior for UX demos.
- Commands: docker compose up --build && tail -f logs/telemetry.log

Telemetry knobs to surface in quickstart:
- sampleRate: 0.1 (default for demos)
- enableTraces: false (on by default for dev)
- token-level cost logging: on (dev-only)
- attach route/model tag (e.g., route: "pico-lab-v1")

Failure modes + recovery checklist (quick):
- 401 errors: confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY scope and rotate keys.
- high latency: switch to warm-start model variant or fall back to short-seq mode.
- truncated streaming: check socket proxies (NGINX chunked vs. unbuffered).
- inconsistent embeddings: verify batch size and model id; rerun with seed=42 to repro.

Ops handoff notes (what to deliver to customer or teammate):
- repo with simple README and one-click run (env example, docker compose)
- small postmortem template for demo glitches
- list of billing/usage safeguards (quota limits, sample-rate telemetry, demo key TTL)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we include a canned local emulator binary vs. fully proxying to hosted? pro: fidelity, con: maintenance. (owner: Jonah)
- Add a one-page cheat sheet with 6 common CLI commands and 4 debug endpoints (owner: Evelyn).
- Decide on default demo model family for labs: rwd-chat-small-v1 or rwd-text-lite? (proposal: small-v1 for better UX).
- Add CI smoke test that runs the 12-minute microflow headlessly and asserts streaming responses are non-empty. (owner: Marcus)

Links & references:
- quickstarter PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starters/pull/42
- related jira: JIRA-DEVEXP-176
- proto doc: confluence:DEVEXP/pico-onramp

Notes to self / quick scribbles:
- Keep the UX friction <= 3 steps to first response.
- Prefer single-file examples for TypeScript + Python so trainers can paste immediately.
- Provide a tiny GIF showing the streaming behavior (helps nontechnical PMs).

End of draft.

Revision log (short):
- 2025-02-11: initial sketch + microflow (Priya)
